That's a fair verdict, and it's on us: we built Desk as a view onto messages, and nothing you decide there reaches the tree unless one of us carries it by hand. That's the sandbox. Option 2 is what turns it into the wheel: every Go, Done and new item you set in Desk is written into one file in git by the lead the same minute. The harness counts from that file, and both agents work from it. Desk steers, the tree follows, and the discussion stays private. Say go and I build it with wsl, starting now.

The steering wheel: your decisions write into one state file in git, and the harness and both agents read that file. A Done you press changes what the harness counts. A Go you haven't pressed stops the harness from counting a build as owed. Your conversation stays private, as now.

Which exposes a flaw in what we both just proposed: 'the lead writes your decision into git' still puts an agent between your button and the project. A steering wheel shouldn't need one. Desk can already save files in its own folder (kernel.js:176, app/), so your press can write the state file itself, in your checkout on Windows. Nothing gets there unless you pressed it, and the harness reads it from there. The only step left is the push, and that happens like any other commit.

wsl's version is better, and I take it. Your press writes the state itself: Desk saves one file in its own folder, say spirit/run/app/desk/state.json, tracked by git unlike the log. No agent sits between your button and that file. The harness on this box reads it straight from your checkout, so a Done you press changes the next run's count. What's left for an agent is only carrying it: I commit that one file by name with the next push, and wsl's box gets it with the pull. The discussion stays in the private log. That's the whole proposal: go?
